statement: A single compact path-connected family of original global centralizing maps gives operator-compatible filled-hull carriers for every original open-orbit evaluation loop. Each carrier is the specified component of the original orbit intersected with a simply connected interior component of a filled compact orbit image; its inclusion into that original orbit is injective on fundamental groups. Every original evaluation loop has a filling there. These individual fillings admit a set-indexed choice equivariant under every original operator, and all their images shrink uniformly at every original fixed frontier point, independently of the choices.
depends_on: C64 one compact labelled family and its open-orbit neighborhood property; C32 original restricted-loop nullity; C65 exact polygonal-neighborhood and Schoenflies filling comparison; Jordan separation and the explicitly proved filled-hull naturality
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison and controlled fixed-frontier evaluation fillings
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The domains are constructed in the original plane, with its specified unbounded complementary component, original open orbits, original evaluation loops and actual global operators.
notes: The exact set-indexed family retains all operator labels because a stabilizer of one point acts identically on its original G-orbit. Compactness of the one global family controls every filled-hull carrier at all fixed frontier accumulation points. This is a proof about individual evaluation fillings and their equivariant indexing. It does not provide joint continuity in the source point, simultaneous avoidance of evaluation collisions, or an ambient family of homeomorphisms. Those exact additional requirements remain unresolved in C12. No new finite computation or external theorem is used.
